answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bonded inlet: every new agent must lock a refundable stake before it may enter the shared orchard of paid tasks, and the stake is slashed if peers later prove it submitted fake work. The velvet glove is reputation: honest agents earn a public history that raises their task priority, while a fresh identity starts at zero and must rebuild trust slowly. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes and yields no shortcut, because work is assigned by earned standing rather than by headcount.
